lines.before: The public 0.1.21 BETA release has the same 20 non-manifest package payload files as exercised 0.1.20. The evidence record covers 0.1.20 runtime observations and the 0.1.21 package comparison; 0.1.21 itself was not separately played in-game. See [current beta evidence and limits](plugins/private_conversation/docs/operator-acceptance.md) and the [0.1.21 release note](https://github.com/Francisco-boop-001/CHIM-PrivateConversation/blob/private_conversation-v0.1.21/distribution/private_conversation-v0.1.21.md).
lines.after: The public 0.1.22 BETA release contains 21 server payload files and changes runtime code. Its [focused verification record](plugins/private_conversation/tasks/critique-fixes-2026-10-20/verification.md) records synthetic test-distro fixture RED/GREEN results and syntax checks; these do not establish a fresh installation, provider run, or Skyrim gameplay session. See [current beta evidence and limits](plugins/private_conversation/docs/operator-acceptance.md) and the [0.1.22 release note](plugins/private_conversation/distribution/private_conversation-v0.1.22.md).

lines.before: Private Conversation’s discovery asset is the flat [`chim-plugin.tar.gz`](https://github.com/Francisco-boop-001/CHIM-PrivateConversation/releases/download/private_conversation-v0.1.21/chim-plugin.tar.gz). The table entry above is the wrapped legacy `private_conversation.tar.gz` route; CHIM’s repository installer strips that configured wrapper, so users should not unpack it by hand. The published BETA release has `prerelease=false` so CHIM can discover it; that flag is a filter, not a maturity certification.
